name: Addo and the Eastern Cape
tagline: A malaria-free safari park where more than 600 elephants come to drink at waterholes, with lions, rhinos and buffalo, and a coast where whales and sharks add to the Big Seven.
highlight: A herd of elephants arriving at a waterhole at dusk, with calves splashing in the mud.
shortDescription: One of South Africa's most rewarding safari parks, malaria-free and easy to reach from Gqeberha, with dense elephant herds, the Big Five, dung beetle crossings and private reserves such as Shamwari.
metaDescription: An Addo Elephant National Park travel guide: elephants at waterholes, the Big Seven, self-drive and guided drives, Shamwari and private reserves, Gqeberha, best time, how to get there and a three-day plan.

intro: Addo Elephant National Park, near Gqeberha, formerly Port Elizabeth, in the Eastern Cape, was established in 1931 to protect the last 11 elephants in the region, which had been hunted almost to extinction. Today it is home to more than 600 elephants and one of the densest elephant populations in Africa, and it is also home to lions, black and white rhinos, buffaloes, spotted hyenas, leopards and a wealth of antelope and birds.

The park has grown to include a marine reserve, with islands where African penguins and Cape gannets breed, and its whales and great white sharks give it the title of the Big Seven. Its main advantage is that it is malaria-free, so there are no tablets to take, and it is easy to reach, only an hour's drive from Gqeberha airport. That makes it a favourite for families and for those adding a safari to a Garden Route trip.

Game viewing at Addo is straightforward. The elephants gather at waterholes within sight of the main camp, and roads through thick, spiky thicket and open grassland allow self-drive exploring. Guided drives at dusk and night increase the chances of seeing lions and hyenas. Nearby private reserves, such as Shamwari and Kwandwe, offer luxury lodges and Big Five safaris, also malaria-free.

whyVisit.intro: Addo is the easiest and most family-friendly place in South Africa for an elephant safari.

points.title: Elephants
points.text: Large herds visit waterholes throughout the day.

points.title: Malaria-free
points.text: No need for tablets, ideal for families and pregnant travellers.

points.title: Easy access
points.text: An hour from Gqeberha, and close to the Garden Route.

points.title: The Big Seven
points.text: Elephants, lions, rhinos, leopards, buffaloes, whales and sharks.

attractionsIntro: The main experiences are game drives, waterholes and the private reserves.

attractions.name: The Hapoor and Domkrag waterholes

image.alt: Elephants walking through the bush in Addo Elephant National Park

attractions.text: Waterholes near the main camp where elephants gather in large numbers in the dry season, viewed from hides or from your vehicle.

attractions.name: Self-drive game drives
attractions.text: Roads through the park allow visitors to look for lions, buffaloes, rhinos, kudu and zebra on their own.
attractions.tip: Ask at the camp where animals have been seen.

attractions.name: Dung beetle crossings
attractions.text: The park has road signs warning of flightless dung beetles, which roll elephant dung across the road.

attractions.name: Guided sunset and night drives
attractions.text: Ranger-led drives in open vehicles, offering the best chance of seeing lions, hyenas and other night animals.

attractions.name: Shamwari and private reserves
attractions.text: Luxury lodges in malaria-free reserves nearby, offering Big Five game drives with rangers, often with rhino and conservation projects.

attractions.name: The marine section and Bird Island
attractions.text: Coastal areas with penguin and gannet colonies, whales and sharks, reached by boat from Gqeberha.

thingsToDoIntro: Game viewing is the main activity, with time for the coast.

thingsToDo.title: Watch elephants at a waterhole
thingsToDo.text: Sit in a hide or vehicle and watch herds drink and bathe.

thingsToDo.title: Go on a guided game drive
thingsToDo.text: Open vehicle drives at dawn, sunset and night.

thingsToDo.title: Try a horseback safari
thingsToDo.text: Ride through the bush near the park.

thingsToDo.title: Visit a private reserve
thingsToDo.text: See rhinos and lions, with luxury.

thingsToDo.title: See penguins and whales
thingsToDo.text: Boat trips from Gqeberha in the bay.

foodIntro: Food in Addo is simple, with farm-style restaurants and braais.

foods.name: Citrus and local produce
foods.text: The Sundays River Valley is a citrus-growing region.

foods.name: Ostrich and game meat
foods.text: Lean meats, in stews and steaks.

foods.name: Seafood
foods.text: Fresh fish and calamari in Gqeberha.

accommodation.intro: Stay in the park, in a nearby guesthouse, or in a luxury lodge.

areas.name: Addo main camp
areas.text: Chalets, cottages and tents in the park.

areas.name: Addo village and guesthouses
areas.text: B&Bs and lodges near the park.

areas.name: Private reserves
areas.text: Lodges in Shamwari, Kwandwe and others.

budget.label: Park entry
budget.value: A daily fee, higher for international visitors

gettingThere.intro: Addo is about 70 km north of Gqeberha.

options.text: Direct flights from Cape Town and Johannesburg.
options.detail: Hire a car at the airport.

options.text: About 2 to 3 hours from Plettenberg Bay.

gettingAround.intro: A car is best for the park.

bestTime.headline: All year, best April–September
bestTime.summary: Addo has a mild climate, with rain at any time of year. The dry winter months have the best game viewing.

seasons.text: Hot and green, with dense bush.
Cool, dry, with animals at waterholes.

bestTime.avoid: The busiest holiday periods in December and January.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you make the most of Addo.
tips: Go in the dry season, from April to September.
Sit at waterholes in the late afternoon.
Watch for dung beetles on the road.
Keep a safe distance from elephants.
Book camps far ahead in holiday periods.

faq.q: How many days do you need at Addo?
faq.a: Two days, or three if you add a private reserve.

faq.q: Can I see the Big Five?
faq.a: Yes, in the park and private reserves.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?

faq.a: By car from Gqeberha, about an hour.

faq.q: Can I visit as a day trip from Gqeberha?
faq.a: Yes, though it is better to stay overnight.
